claim.claim-text: 1. A method of preparing a semiconductor substrate, the semiconductor substrate comprising two major, generally parallel surfaces, one of which is a front surface of the semiconductor substrate and the other of which is a back surface of the semiconductor substrate, and a circumferential edge joining the front and back semiconductor substrate surfaces, the method comprising:

2. The method of claim 1 wherein the semiconductor substrate comprises a semiconductor wafer, optionally wherein the semiconductor wafer comprises a material selected from the group consisting of silicon, gallium arsenide, silicon carbide, silicon germanium, silicon nitride, silicon dioxide, and germanium, and combinations thereof.
3. The method of any one of claims 1 or 2, wherein
4. The method of any one of claims 1 to 3, wherein the carbon-rich polymer layer has a thickness between about 1 nanometer and about 100 nanometers thick.
5. The method of any one of claims 1 to 4, wherein
6. The method of any one of claims 1 to 5, wherein the second metal film comprises a metal having a carbon solubility of at least about 0.05 atomic % at 1000°C.
7. The method of any one of claims 1 to 6, wherein the second metal film comprises a metal having a carbon solubility of less than about 3 atomic % at 1000°C.

8. The method of any one of claims 1 to 7, wherein the second metal film comprises a metal selected from the group consisting of nickel, copper, iron, platinum, palladium, ruthenium, cobalt and alloys thereof, optionally wherein the second metal film comprises nickel or copper.

9. A multilayer article comprising: a semiconductor wafer comprising two major, generally parallel surfaces, one of which is a front surface of the semiconductor wafer and the other of which is a back surface of the semiconductor wafer, and a circumferential edge joining the front and back surfaces, wherein the semiconductor wafer comprises a material selected from the group consisting of silicon, gallium arsenide, silicon carbide, silicon germanium, germanium, and any combination thereof; and

(a) a first layer of graphene in contact with the front surface of the semiconductor wafer; a layer of boron nitride in contact with the first layer of graphene; and a second layer of graphene in contact with the layer of boron nitride; or (b) a first layer of boron nitride in contact with the front surface of the semiconductor wafer; a layer of graphene in contact with the layer of boron nitride; and a second layer of boron nitride in contact with the layer of graphene.
10. The multilayer article of claim 9, wherein the semiconductor wafer is a single crystal silicon wafer sliced from a single crystal silicon ingot grown by the Czochralski method.

11. The multilayer article of claim 9 or claim 10, wherein the front surface of the semiconductor wafer comprises a dielectric layer, optionally wherein the dielectric layer comprises silicon dioxide or silicon nitride, or both silicon dioxide and silicon nitride.

12. The multilayer article of any one of claims 9 to 11, further comprising a metal film in contact with the second layer of graphene or the second layer of boron nitride, the metal film comprising a front metal film surface, a back metal film surface, and a bulk metal region between the front and back metal film surfaces.

13. The multilayer article of claim 12, wherein the metal film comprises a metal selected from the group consisting of nickel, copper, iron, platinum, palladium, ruthenium, cobalt, and alloys thereof.
14. The multilayer article of any of claims 9-13, wherein the layer of graphene comprises between about 2 and about 50 mono-atomically thick layers of graphene.
15. The multilayer article of any of claims 9-13, wherein the layer of boron nitride comprises between about 2 and about 100 mono-atomically thick layers of boron nitride.
